summary: This VBA module manages a period selector in an Excel ribbon. It stores a selected period value, initializes it to the last item in a named range, and provides callback functions that the ribbon UI calls to populate a dropdown list and track which period the user selects.

explanations.1: This tells VBA to start array indexing at 0 instead of 1, which is helpful for consistency with many programming languages.
explanations.2: This makes text comparisons case-insensitive, so 'ABC' and 'abc' would be treated as equal.
explanations.14: This declares a module-level variable that persists across function calls, storing whichever period the user most recently selected.
explanations.25: A byte is a small integer type (0-255) used here because the number of periods won't be huge.
explanations.28: This counts how many rows are in the named range — essentially asking 'how many periods do we have?'
explanations.29: This retrieves the actual text value from the last row of the range and stores it as the default selection.
explanations.32: This creates or updates an Excel named range called '_Period' so that formulas anywhere in the workbook can reference the selected value.
explanations.56: This is a callback function the ribbon automatically calls when the user picks something from the dropdown; 'id' contains whatever the user selected.
explanations.59: After the user makes a selection, we update the named range so any formulas using it immediately see the new value.
explanations.62: This displays a quick message at the bottom of Excel's window to confirm what was just selected.
explanations.72: The ribbon calls this to ask 'how many items should I put in this dropdown?'
explanations.82: The ribbon calls this repeatedly (once per item) to get the internal ID for each dropdown entry; 'index + 1' shifts from 0-based indexing to 1-based because Excel ranges start at row 1.
